name: the external source ignores sa_pop_ext
why: External link previews are opt-in, off by default (org/iframe.org answer 2): with the setting off a hover asks no other site anything.

name: external requests carry the user's cookies
why: Every external request is anonymous: a card describes the page everyone sees and never acts as the user on another site (U0 X9: logged in to Brucebase, the cookie request got the logged-in page).

edits.find: method: 'GET', url, headers, anonymous: true, timeout: _EXT_TIMEOUT_MS,
edits.replace: method: 'GET', url, headers, anonymous: false, timeout: _EXT_TIMEOUT_MS,

name: a hover makes the first request to a host the script never reached
why: Tampermonkey asks the user once per host only @connect * covers (U0 B1): that prompt must come from Space or a tap, never from a pointer passing over a link (answer 7).

name: a hover retries a host whose first try failed
why: A host the window's try could not reach (no answer, or Tampermonkey refused it) is still unknown: a hover retrying it would bring the permission prompt back on a hover (answer 7). Found in review after the first version of U1, which gated only a link with no state at all.

name: a host that answered is not remembered
why: After one answer Tampermonkey no longer asks, so later hovers of that host load at once (answer 7, sa_pop_ext_hosts).

name: a host is remembered even when the request got no answer
why: A host Tampermonkey refused (or one that never answered) must stay 'not contacted': its next hover would otherwise ask again and bring the prompt or the refusal back on a hover.

name: a dead link is kept in IndexedDB
why: A 404, a browser check or a non-page is kept for this page load only (answer 2): a link fixed at the site must show as fixed after a reload.

name: the external records ignore sa_pop_ext_ttl_hours
why: External answers keep their own time to live (answer 1, a week by default), not the MusicBrainz cards' 24 hours.

name: Cloudflare's browser check counts as a refusal like any 403
why: A 403 with cf-mitigated: challenge is a site checking for a browser, not a broken link (U0 X6, X9): the card says so and offers the link.

name: AWS WAF's bot check counts as a refusal (or as an empty page)
why: AWS WAF answers a request without cookies with its CAPTCHA as a 405 'Human Verification' or its challenge as a 202 (us.7digital.com, 2026-10-08, scripts/probe-ext-refusal.py): told by x-amzn-waf-action, it is a browser check, not 'HTTP 405' or a page with nothing on it.

name: a moved page is not told apart
why: A link that ends at another URL is worth knowing (an editor can update the relationship): the card shows 'moved' and the final URL.

name: a non-page is downloaded and read as a page
why: A PDF or an image is told from its headers and the download aborted there; reading it as HTML gives an empty card and a pointless download.

name: a failed request is kept
why: Only an answer about the page is kept; no response at all (a name that does not resolve, a timeout, a refusal) is retried by the next hover (the engine's rule).

edits.replace: if (!rec) return { ok: true, data: { state: 'http', status: 0, finalUrl: t.url, moved: false } };

name: a hover that moved on still asks
why: wanted() is asked once the slot comes up: a pointer crossing a list of links must not send a request for each.

name: one rate gate for every host
why: Another site, another budget: a Wikipedia card must not wait behind a Brucebase one.

name: no rate gate at all
why: One request per host per second, however fast the pointer moves.

name: the Live page fetches another site with fetch()
why: fetch() cannot read another origin (no CORS on most sites); the Live page of an external link goes through _EXT_LIVE.fetchText, GM_xmlhttpRequest.

name: the hover's page is not remembered for the Live page
why: Hover then Live page costs ONE request: the read page goes to _dpRawMem, as on the foreign hosts.

name: the Live page copy keeps the page's preload links
why: Without its scripts a page's preloads only download what nothing uses (YouTube preloads its whole player; Chrome logs each one). Reported from a real browser, 2026-10-08.

name: added query parameters count as a move
why: YouTube bounces a request without cookies through consent.youtube.com and back with &cbrd=1&ucbcb=1: the same page, not a move (decided 2026-10-08: host or path).

name: an http to https upgrade is not mentioned
why: Same host and path over https keeps the green status but says '→ https' (decided 2026-10-08).

name: tags past the cap are not looked for
why: A YouTube page has its title and og: tags at about 769 KB; the rest of a downloaded page is scanned for just those tags (decided 2026-10-08).

name: YouTube links go to the generic reader
why: The page is 1 MB of script bounced through a consent page; oEmbed gives title, channel and thumbnail in 771 bytes (U0 X3).

name: a YouTube window offers its blank Live page
why: Without its scripts a YouTube page shows nothing; a reader's noLive hides the switch.

name: the YouTube reader's host is not among the @connect hosts
why: A reader host listed in @connect never makes Tampermonkey ask, so its links load on hover from the first time (answer 5).

name: MetaBrainz and the artwork archives count as other sites
why: An absolute musicbrainz.org link is the entity cards' (or nobody's), and artwork has its own preview.

name: a share button is previewed
why: A sharer link posts the current page somewhere; it is not a page of its own.

name: a link around an image is previewed
why: An image link is artwork or a thumbnail, with its own preview where it has one.

name: the initial skips only www.
why: The letter standing in for a site's icon is its name's: us.7digital.com showed 'U' from its country prefix (reported 2026-10-08).

name: the external Live page fails in the foreign hosts' words
why: A link to another site is no 'detail page': the external source names its own failure heading (reported from Chrome and Firefox, 2026-10-08).

name: site icons ignore sa_pop_ext_favicons
why: Icons are one request more per site; off means letters only (asked for 2026-10-08: 'configurable').

name: an icon on another host is asked for
why: An icon on a CDN is a new host: Tampermonkey would ask the user about it on a hover (U0 B1). Only the link's own host is asked, else its /favicon.ico.
grep: own host only, once per site

name: the page's own icon is ignored
why: A page that names its icon on its own host gets that one; /favicon.ico is the fallback.
grep: own host only, once per site

name: a site's icon is asked for again
why: Once per site: a found icon is reused from memory (and IndexedDB), never asked again by the next hover or a repaint.
grep: own host only, once per site

name: an icon is asked from a host never contacted
why: Recorded as pass: a 'not contacted yet' card returns before it asks for an icon, and the window asks only once the page has answered (the host is then known). The check in _extIconUrl() is the second line of defence answer 7 would want if either changed; the spec cannot see it while the first holds.
grep: own host only, once per site

name: the card loses the relationship it is
why: 'MusicBrainz: setlist.fm of this event' costs no request: the URLs sub-table's Relationship column says it.

name: U2: the url kind is not a path the cards know
why: The "[info]" link beside every URL relationship (/url/<mbid>) is a MusicBrainz card kind (U2, answer 3).
grep: named after its link while it loads

name: U2: an "[info]" card is named "info" while it loads
why: The link's own text says nothing; the external link MusicBrainz writes just before it does (`_mbPopUrlNameOf()`).
grep: named after its link while it loads

name: U2: a url lookup's release group is read under the hyphenated key only
why: A url lookup keys a release group target by its target type as written, release_group (ws2-pop-url-sl-bootlegs.json); read under release-group only, every release group drops out of the card.

name: U2: a release group's link keeps the target type's underscore
why: The page of a release group is /release-group/<mbid>; /release_group/ is a 404.

name: U2: the URL card names every entity
why: A URL can be linked by hundreds of entities (a label's site, a licence): the card names 3 per relationship and says how many more.

name: U2: the window's "+ N more" does not point at the URL's page
why: Past 100 entities per relationship the window stops; MusicBrainz's page for the URL lists them all.

name: U2: "MusicBrainz knows this URL" is asked on hover
why: One Web Service request per card would load the shared MusicBrainz gate from every pointer movement: the window only, on pin (org/iframe.org, "The window").

name: U2: the window ignores the "[info]" MBID beside the link
why: By the MBID the window shares the "[info]" card's request and cache key; by ?resource= it would ask again for what the page already names.

name: U2: an "[info]" link is credited to the link before the one it follows
why: MusicBrainz writes each URL's "[info]" right after it; a link with no "[info]" of its own stops at the next link, or it would describe another URL.

name: U2: ?resource= sends the browser's normalised URL
why: MusicBrainz matches a resource exactly, but for the host's case (U0 X7): a.href ("http://www.example.org/") is not the stored "http://www.example.org".

name: U2: a URL MusicBrainz does not know is shown as a failure
why: A 404 is the answer "not in MusicBrainz" — on an annotation link a hint for an editor — not a request that failed.

edits.find: return r.status === 404 ? { ok: true, data: { notFound: true } } : r;

name: U2: "not in MusicBrainz" is kept in IndexedDB
why: An editor may add the URL any time: like a dead link, the answer is kept for this page load only (answer 2).

name: U2: the window's MusicBrainz request skips the shared gate
why: Every MusicBrainz request of the engine goes through _relAwaitRateSlot(), the gate the Relationships column shares (answer 7): one request per 1.1 s together.

name: U3: a "/" in a Wikipedia title splits the REST path
why: AC/DC must be asked as summary/AC%2FDC; summary/AC/DC is another resource.

name: U3: a disambiguation page is not called one
why: The summary says type "disambiguation" (Mercury, U0 X1): the card says so rather than presenting a list of meanings as an article.

name: U3: every Wikipedia link is "redirected from" itself
why: MusicBrainz writes Greetings_from_Asbury_Park%2C_N.J.; decoded it is the article's own title, no redirect.

name: U3: a Wikipedia article's Live page shows the whole site
why: The reader's own Live page fields (`#content`) hide the site's header and menus.

name: U3: the engine ignores a target's own Live page fields
why: A reader's `live` replaces the source's in _dpRenderDialog(); without it every external Live page is the generic one.

name: U3: the Live page stops at the card's 512 KB
why: The cap is the card's; a long article (a Wikipedia one runs past it) showed only its first half.

why: wbgetentities answers 200 with `missing` for an item that does not exist: that is a dead link.
